title: A refused commit leaves your paths staged in the shared index, and only the next node can see it
body:
**A HOOK THAT REJECTS A COMMIT LEAVES THE COMMITTER'S PATHS STAGED IN THE SHARED INDEX, AND NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS SO.** `git commit` stages nothing and unstages nothing when a pre-commit hook exits non-zero, so the `git add` that preceded it stands. In a single shared checkout the index is shared state: those paths are then exposed to every other node's next commit until the owner lands or unstages them.

**IT IS INVISIBLE TO THE PERSON WHO CAUSED IT AND VISIBLE ONLY TO THE NEXT NODE.** From inside the refusing session it reads as a commit that did not happen; there is no message about the index, and no reason to think about it while diagnosing why the gate refused. Measured 2026-08-30: ic's `tui.rs` and `tui/focus.rs` sat staged across two gate refusals and a hook-source investigation, and **dc found them from the outside**, in `git diff --cached` after staging their own paths.

**WHAT PREVENTED HARM WAS `--only`, NOT CARE.** `git commit --only <paths>` builds its tree from HEAD plus the named paths and ignores the rest of the index, so dc's `07d49a2e` carried their eight files and none of ic's. **A bare `git commit` would have carried another node's in-flight work under dc's message, silently, with no error available to give** -- the thing three nodes each separately refused to do to one another that same morning.

**THIS IS TRUE OF EVERY GATE REFUSAL, not of the rustfmt arm that surfaced it.** The rustfmt module-resolution defect (probe rename breaking `mod` lookup) is fixed separately and is not this. Any hook that exits non-zero for any reason -- clock guard, header guard, critic gate, canon check -- leaves the same residue.

**WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED HERE:** the candidate remedies are not obviously equivalent and at least one is destructive. Printing a warning naming the still-staged paths on refusal is cheap and non-destructive. Auto-unstaging on refusal is NOT safe -- it would discard a deliberate partial-add the committer intends to keep, and `git add -p` work is not recoverable from the index once dropped. **The shape of the fix is a decision, not a detail.**

Related: the `--only` habit is currently the entire margin between nodes and each other's bytes in a shared checkout, and it has no diagnostic behind it. This issue does not propose changing that, but it is the same surface.
